retained_approvals.name: fresh decision binds an earlier authenticated approval after its credential expires
retained_approvals.scope: Cryptographic and exact-binding observations only. This does not execute stateful admission, authorize an effect, establish safe response routing, or prove runtime retention.
retained_approvals.decision_key_note: The fresh decision uses the P-256 public test key certified as party:ada rather than Ada's earlier Ed25519 key. The fixture trust policy explicitly permits this subject; this does not select a universal namespace or rotation policy.

trust_policy_scope: The permitted-subject lists illustrate the governed principal-name model with explicitly constrained issuer/key/name authority. They are TEST policy, not a normative deployment configuration API. A certificate must verify under a permitted key that itself has authority for the claimed subject; scopes are not unioned across issuers or keys. Deliberately overlapping authority identifies the same governed principal. An empty subject set grants no naming authority.
jcs_scope: The four JCS cases test RFC8785 canonicalization primitives only. They are not whole-message admission examples; some numeric inputs deliberately exceed the core's safe integral-valued-number bound.
